newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin in good form, no early election - Nemtsov.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin in good form, no early election - Nemtsov.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin is in good health and Russians will not have to elect a successor before his term in office expires in the year 2000, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Wednesday.

"The next presidential election will be in the year 2000, I promise you that," Nemtsov told reporters during a trip to the city of Nizhny Novgorod where he served as governor before Yeltsin appointed him to the cabinet earlier this year.

Yeltsin, who has staged a strong political comeback after recovering from open heart surgery and pneumonia, is now holidaying in lakeside resort in the northwestern region of Karelia near the Finnish border.
"Yesterday I met the president (in Karelia). He feels well...All day we worked together and everything was fine," said Nemtsov, once described by Yeltsin himself as a possible future president.

Nemtsov said he had jokingly told Yeltsin he was fit enough to visit the sauna regularly and to beat his companions with the customary cluster of birch twigs used in Russian bath houses to help stimulate blood circulation.

Yeltsin will go fishing in a lake and visit the island of Kizhi on Thursday, Itar-Tass news agency said. The trip had originally been planned for Wednesday but had to be cancelled due to bad weather in the area, it added.
Yeltsin is a keen angler and his wife Naina said this week that he had already caught a lot of fish during his holiday, which started last Sunday.
But he has not indulged in his other favourite sport, tennis, presumably because of the likely strain it would put on his heart.

The presidential press service in Moscow said Yeltsin would receive Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari next Saturday and Sunday at his holiday residence. It said the two men would discuss bilateral relations and international issues.
